β3 = E[D⊥Y]/E[D⊥²] with E[D⊥Y]=E[D⊥ m0(X)]+E[D⊥D τ(X)].
E[D⊥D τ(X)]>0 but E[D⊥ m0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a0-a1X)m0(X)]≠0 in general, zero iff p(X) is linear in X. With non-linear p(·) and non-linear m0(·) the first term can be arbitrarily negative and dominate.
E.g. X∈{-1,0,1} equiprobable, p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3, m0(x)=x², τ≡0.1>0 gives E[D⊥Y]<0 so β3<0 despite E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=τ(X)>0 a.s.
The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect is E[τ(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0 with residual D-E[D|X]. OLS uses the linear residual D-Π1,X D, which is not orthogonal to m0(X) without extra linearity.

Hence under the stated no-parametric-assumptions restriction positivity of the population linear D coefficient is forced only under unconditional randomisation. Case 2 and Case 3 can be negative even with τ_i>0 a.s.

Current room consensus is A. Only Case 1. Earlier E view for Case 3 requires non-parametric control for X or linearity of p(X), which is not allowed by the problem statement. The nuance that non-parametric control would preserve sign remains noted.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y(0)\mid X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau\mid X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1\mid X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $E[Y\mid D,X]=m_{0}(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D\mid X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. 
$\beta_{1}=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$.
The $1+D$ linear projection is the ATE. Sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general.
$\beta_{2}=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[\tau\mid D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)\mid D=0]$.
Selection bias can dominate. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_{0}(0)=0$, $m_{0}(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_{2}= \varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Marginal $Y\sim1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$ uses the linear residual $D_{\perp}=D-a_{0}-a_{1}X$.
$\beta_{3}=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^{2}]$, $E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_{0}-a_{1}X)m_{0}(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot),m_{0}(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative.
E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_{3}<0$ despite $E[Y\mid D=1,X]-E[Y\mid D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect is $E[\tau(X)v(X)]/E[v(X)]>0$ with $v(X)=p(1-p)$, i.e. with residual $D-E[D\mid X]$. The OLS residual $D-\Pi_{1,X}D$ is not orthogonal to $m_{0}(X)$ under misspecification, so sign reversal is possible.

Earlier round disagreement about Case 3 using the non-parametric residual $D-E[D\mid X]$ is resolved: the question asks for the linear projection on $1,D,X$, not the non-parametric partial effect.

All colleagues in round 3 now agree. Current belief: positivity of the population OLS $D$ coefficient is forced only under unconditional randomisation. Answer A. Only Case 1.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: Potential outcome $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $D\perp (Y(0),Y(1))|X$,
$E[Y|D,X]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$, ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp (Y(0),Y(1))$. Linear projection on $\{1,D\}$ is mean difference
$\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation forces sign.

Case 2 $D\perp (Y(0),Y(1))|X$ but $D\not\perp X$ generally.
$\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection term can dominate. Example $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$.
Sign not forced.

Case 3 regression $Y\sim1+D+X$ is linear projection onto span$\{1,D,X\}$.
Write $D_{\perp}=D-a_0-a_1X$ the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$.
$\beta_3=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^2]$, $E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_0(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_{\perp}m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot)$ and $m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate.
Example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equal mass, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_3<0$ despite $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

That is the Frisch-Waugh quantity colleagues 4,5,7 invoked for Case 3. It is not the OLS coefficient with $X$ entered linearly, $D_{\perp}=D-\Pi_{1,X}D$. With a fully flexible control of $X$ Case 3 would be sign-protected; under the stated linear control it is not.

Current round 3 consensus is A. Only Case 1. Earlier E arguments rely on the non-parametric partial effect, not the stated linear specification. No unresolved issues for the stated linear specification; positivity of the OLS $D$ coefficient is forced only by unconditional randomisation.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The potential-outcome set-up is $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$ with $\tau>0$ a.s., $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $m_{0}(X)=E[Y(0)|X]$, $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$. Conditional unconfoundedness gives $E[Y|D,X]=m_{0}(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=\tau(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$ pointwise.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp (Y(0),Y(1))$.
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation makes the $1+D$ linear projection the ATE. Sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp (Y(0),Y(1))|X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general.
$\beta_{2}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
Selection term $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ can be made arbitrarily negative by $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$. Example $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_{0}(0)=0$, $m_{0}(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_{2}=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$. Marginal $Y\sim1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. OLS on $1,D,X$ is the linear projection $\beta_{3}=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^{2}]$ with $D_{\perp}=D-a_{0}-a_{1}X$ the residual of $D$ from its linear projection on $1,X$, not the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$.
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]>0$, but $E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_{0}-a_{1}X)m_{0}(X)]$ is zero only if $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot)$ and $m_{0}(\cdot)$ the first term can dominate and be arbitrarily negative. E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_{3}<0$, although $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect is $E[\tau(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0$ with residual $D-E[D|X]$. The linear misspecification breaks orthogonality to $m_{0}(X)$.

Earlier dissent claimed Case 3 is sign-protected, conflating the non-parametric partial effect with the linear projection on $1,D,X$. Current round 3 consensus, and my current belief, is that positivity of the population OLS $D$ coefficient is forced only by unconditional randomisation.

Current belief: A. Only Case 1.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population OLS coefficient is the $L^2$ linear projection onto the regressors actually included, not the non-parametric conditional mean.

Write $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)\mid X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau\mid X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1\mid X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $E[Y\mid D,X]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D\mid X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. Then $D\perp X$ and
$\beta_1=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation makes the $1+D$ projection the ATE; sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general.
$\beta_2=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[\tau\mid D=1]+E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$.
Selection bias $E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$ can dominate $E[\tau\mid D=1]$. With $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$, $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Marginal $1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$: $\beta_3=E[D_\perp Y]/E[D_\perp^2]$ with $D_\perp=D-a_0-a_1X$ the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$.
$E[D_\perp Y]=E[D_\perp m_0(X)]+E[D_\perp D\,\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_\perp D\,\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_\perp m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot)$ and non-linear $m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative. Example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equal mass, $p(-1)=0.2$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1>0$ gives $E[D_\perp Y]<0$, $\beta_3<0$ despite $\tau(X)>0$ a.s. and $E[Y\mid D=1,X]-E[Y\mid D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$.

The sign-protected quantity under conditional unconfoundedness is the non-parametric partial effect $E[\tau(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0$ obtained with residual $D-E[D\mid X]$. OLS with linear control $1,X$ uses $D-\Pi_{1,X}D$ and is not orthogonal to $m_0(X)$ without linearity restrictions on $p$ and $m_0$.

Hence positivity of the population OLS $D$ coefficient is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can be made negative with $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

Current belief is Only Case 1 must be positive, option A. Round 3 consensus is unanimous A; earlier dissent that Case 3 is sign-protected with linear $X$ is resolved as linear-misspecification / residual orthogonality failure. No remaining support for options E / F / G.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: Potential-outcome form $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., under conditional unconfoundedness $E[Y\mid X,D]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$ with $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)\mid X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau\mid X]>0$ a.s., $p(X)=P(D=1\mid X)$. Population OLS is the $L^2$ linear projection on the regressors actually included.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. Then $D\perp X$ and $\beta_1=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation makes the intercept-slope projection the ATE; sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general. $\beta_2=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[\tau\mid D=1]+E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$. Selection bias can dominate $\tau$. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Marginal $1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$. $\beta_3=E[D_\perp Y]/E[D_\perp^2]$ with $D_\perp=D-a_0-a_1X$ the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$. $E[D_\perp Y]=E[D_\perp m_0(X)]+E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]$. $E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_\perp m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot),m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative. E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1>0$ gives $E[D_\perp Y]<0$, $\beta_3<0$ although $E[Y\mid D=1,X]-E[Y\mid D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

The non-parametric partial effect $E[\tau(X)w(X)]/E[w(X)]$, $w(X)=p(X)(1-p(X))>0$, obtained with residual $D-E[D\mid X]$, is $>0$, but that is not the OLS coefficient with $X$ entered linearly. Earlier colleagues 4,5,7 obtained $\beta_3>0$ by effectively replacing $D_\perp$ with $D-E[D\mid X]$, i.e. assuming linearity of $E[D\mid X]$ and $m_0(X)$, an extra parametric restriction forbidden.

In round 3 all eight colleagues now agree the linear projection on $1,D,X$ is not sign identified under unconfoundedness alone, and sign reversal is possible in Cases 2 and 3. Positivity of the individual effect is preserved by the unconditional mean difference, and by the non-parametric partial effect, but not by the OLS coefficients in Cases 2 and 3.

Current best belief remains A. Only Case 1 is guaranteed positive in population OLS.

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population coefficient is the $L^2$ linear projection on the regressors actually included. Write $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $E[Y|D,X]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$.

Case1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. Then $D\perp X$ and
$\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation makes the $1+D$ projection the ATE. Sign forced.

Case2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))|X$ but $D\not\perp X$ generally.
$\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection bias $E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$ can dominate the positive $\tau$ term. Example $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0,m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for $M$ large. Marginal $Y\sim1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$. Let $D_\perp=D-a_0-a_1X$ be the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$, $\beta_3=E[D_\perp Y]/E[D_\perp^2]$.
$E[D_\perp Y]=E[D_\perp m_0(X)]+E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_\perp m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot),m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate the $\tau$ part. Example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1>0$ gives $E[D_\perp Y]<0$ so $\beta_3<0$ although $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect $E[\tau(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0$ is obtained with residual $D-E[D|X]$, not with the linear residual $D-\Pi_{1,X}D$ used by OLS on $1,D,X$. Orthogonality to $m_0(X)$ is lost under linear control when $p(X)$ is non-linear.

Earlier disagreement about Case3 being sign-protected via Frisch-Waugh is resolved: the question asks for the linear projection on $1,D,X$, not the non-parametric partial effect, and sign reversal is possible under unrestricted non-linear $m_0$ and $p$.

Thus positivity of the individual effect is preserved only by the unconditional randomised mean difference. Conditional randomisation protects the conditional mean difference but not the marginal OLS slope in Case2 nor the linear partial coefficient in Case3 under non-parametric restrictions.

Current belief: only Case1 must be strictly positive in population; Cases2 and3 can be made negative with $\tau_i>0$ a.s. Answer A. Only Case1.

The problem is $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y(0)\mid X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau\mid X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1\mid X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $E[Y\mid D,X]=m_{0}(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D\mid X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. 
$\beta_{1}=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$.
The $1+D$ linear projection is the ATE. Sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general.
$\beta_{2}=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[\tau\mid D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)\mid D=0]$.
Selection bias can dominate. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_{0}(0)=0$, $m_{0}(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_{2}= \varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Marginal $Y\sim1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$ uses the linear residual $D_{\perp}=D-a_{0}-a_{1}X$.
$\beta_{3}=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^{2}]$, $E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_{0}-a_{1}X)m_{0}(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot),m_{0}(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative.
E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_{3}<0$ despite $E[Y\mid D=1,X]-E[Y\mid D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect is $E[\tau(X)v(X)]/E[v(X)]>0$ with $v(X)=p(1-p)$, i.e. with residual $D-E[D\mid X]$. The OLS residual $D-\Pi_{1,X}D$ is not orthogonal to $m_{0}(X)$ under misspecification, so sign reversal is possible.

Earlier round disagreement about Case 3 using the non-parametric residual $D-E[D\mid X]$ is resolved: the question asks for the linear projection on $1,D,X$, not the non-parametric partial effect.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp (Y(0),Y(1))$.
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation makes the $1+D$ linear projection the ATE. Sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp (Y(0),Y(1))|X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general.
$\beta_{2}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
Selection term $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ can be made arbitrarily negative by $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$. Example $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_{0}(0)=0$, $m_{0}(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_{2}=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$. Marginal $Y\sim1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. OLS on $1,D,X$ is the linear projection $\beta_{3}=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^{2}]$ with $D_{\perp}=D-a_{0}-a_{1}X$ the residual of $D$ from its linear projection on $1,X$, not the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$.
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]>0$, but $E[D_{\perp}m_{0}(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_{0}-a_{1}X)m_{0}(X)]$ is zero only if $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot)$ and $m_{0}(\cdot)$ the first term can dominate and be arbitrarily negative. E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_{3}<0$, although $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect is $E[\tau(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0$ with residual $D-E[D|X]$. The linear misspecification breaks orthogonality to $m_{0}(X)$. The earlier dissent that Case 3 is sign-protected conflated the non-parametric partial effect with the linear projection on $1,D,X$.

Current round 4 consensus is unanimous for A. Only unconditional randomisation forces a strictly positive population OLS coefficient on $D$. Conditional randomisation alone does not protect the marginal $1+D$ coefficient, and linear control for $X$ does not protect the linear $D$ coefficient without functional form restrictions on $p(X)$ and $m_{0}(X)$. Current belief: A. Only Case 1.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: I am working with potential outcomes $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)\mid X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau\mid X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1\mid X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $D\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$, $E[Y\mid D,X]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D\mid X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. Linear projection on $\{1,D\}$ is the mean difference
$\beta_1=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation forces the sign.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$ but $D\not\perp X$ generally.
$\beta_2=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[\tau\mid D=1]+E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$ can dominate. Example $X\in\{0,1\}$,
$p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Sign not forced.

Case 3 regression $Y\sim1+D+X$ is linear projection onto span $\{1,D,X\}$.
$\beta_3=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^2]$ with $D_{\perp}=D-a_0-a_1X$ the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$.
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_0(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_{\perp}m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$.
With non-linear $p(\cdot)$ and $m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate.
Example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equal mass, $p(-1)=0.2,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_3<0$ despite $E[Y\mid D=1,X]-E[Y\mid D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect is
$\beta^{np}=E[\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))]/E[p(X)(1-p(X))]>0$ with residual $D-E[D\mid X]$.
That is the Frisch-Waugh quantity invoked in earlier E arguments. It is not the OLS coefficient with $X$ entered linearly, $D_{\perp}=D-\Pi_{1,X}D$. With a fully flexible control of $X$ Case 3 would be sign protected; under the stated linear control it is not.

Current round 4 discussion is unanimous for the stated linear specification: positivity of the population OLS $D$ coefficient is forced only by unconditional randomisation. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all now give A. Only Case 1. Earlier E arguments rely on the non-parametric partial effect rather than the stated linear specification. No unresolved issues for the stated linear specification.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: Potential-outcome form $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$, $E[Y|D,X]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$, ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$. Population OLS is the $L^2$ linear projection on the regressors actually included.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$, hence $D\perp X$. 
$\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$. 
Unconditional randomisation makes the $1+D$ projection the ATE; sign forced.

Case 2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))|X$ but marginal dependence on $X$ remains.
$\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection bias $E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$ can dominate $\tau$.
E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Marginal $1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$. $\beta_3=E[D_\perp Y]/E[D_\perp^2]$ with $D_\perp=D-a_0-a_1X$ the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$.
$E[D_\perp Y]=E[D_\perp m_0(X)]+E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_\perp m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ vanishes iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot),m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative.
E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=0.2$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1>0$ gives $E[D_\perp Y]<0$, $\beta_3<0$ although $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ a.s.

The non-parametric partial effect $E[\tau(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0$ obtained with residual $D-E[D|X]$ is positive, but that is not the OLS coefficient when $X$ is entered linearly. Earlier claims for Case 3 positivity used $D-E[D|X]$ or implicitly assumed linearity of $p(X)$ and $m_0(X)$; under the stated no-parametric-assumptions restriction the linear projection is not sign identified.

In round 4 all eight colleagues now give A. Only the unconditional randomised regression is guaranteed $>0$ in population OLS. Positivity fails in Cases 2 and 3 under unconfoundedness alone.

Current best belief: A. Only Case 1.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population OLS coefficient is the L² linear projection on the regressors actually included, not the non-parametric conditional mean.

Write $Y=Y(0)+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_0(X)=E[Y(0)\mid X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau\mid X]>0$, $p(X)=P(D=1\mid X)$. Under conditional unconfoundedness $E[Y\mid D,X]=m_0(X)+D\tau(X)$ and ${\rm Cov}(Y,D\mid X)=\tau(X)p(X)(1-p(X))>0$.

Case 1. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))$. Then $D\perp X$ and
$\beta_1=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation makes the $1+D$ projection the ATE; sign is forced.

Case 2. $D\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid X$ but $D\not\perp X$ in general.
$\beta_2=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[\tau\mid D=1]+E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$.
Selection bias $E[m_0(X)\mid D=1]-E[m_0(X)\mid D=0]$ can dominate $E[\tau\mid D=1]$.
Example $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=M$, $\tau\equiv\varepsilon>0$ gives $\beta_2=\varepsilon-0.8M<0$ for large $M$. Marginal $1+D$ is not sign protected.

Case 3. Projection on $\{1,D,X\}$: $\beta_3=E[D_{\perp}Y]/E[D_{\perp}^2]$ with $D_{\perp}=D-a_0-a_1X$ the linear residual of $D$ on $1,X$.
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[D_{\perp}m_0(X)]+E[D_{\perp}D\,\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_{\perp}D\,\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_{\perp}m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. With non-linear $p(\cdot)$ and non-linear $m_0(\cdot)$ the first term can be made arbitrarily negative.
Example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equal mass, $p(-1)=0.2$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.3$, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $\tau\equiv0.1>0$ gives $E[D_{\perp}Y]<0$, $\beta_3<0$ despite $\tau(X)>0$ a.s. and $E[Y\mid D=1,X]-E[Y\mid D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$.

The sign-protected non-parametric partial effect under unconfoundedness is $E[\tau(X)p(1-p)]/E[p(1-p)]>0$ obtained with residual $D-E[D\mid X]$. OLS with linear control $1,X$ uses $D-\Pi_{1,X}D$ and is not orthogonal to $m_0(X)$ without linearity restrictions on $p$ and $m_0$.

Hence positivity of the population OLS $D$ coefficient is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can be made negative with $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

Current belief is Only Case 1 must be positive, option A. Round 4 consensus is unanimous A across all 8 colleagues; earlier dissent in round 0 favouring E / F / G for Case 3 is resolved as linear-misspecification / residual orthogonality failure. No remaining support for options E/F/G.

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population coefficient is the $L^2$ linear projection on the regressors actually included. $\beta_2=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection bias $E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$ can dominate the positive $\tau$ term.

$E[D_\perp Y]=E[D_\perp m_0(X)]+E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]$.
$E[D_\perp D\tau(X)]>0$ but $E[D_\perp m_0(X)]=E[(p(X)-a_0-a_1X)m_0(X)]$ is zero iff $p(X)$ is linear in $X$. Earlier round disagreement: some colleagues argued Case3 is sign-protected via Frisch-Waugh / $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]>0$. That is true for the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$, but the question asks for the linear projection on $1,D,X$. Under unrestricted non-linear $m_0$ and $p$, sign reversal is possible.

All colleagues in round 4 now converge on A. Only Case1 must be strictly positive in population; Cases2 and3 can be made negative with $\tau_i>0$ a.s. Current belief: Answer A. Only Case1.
